title: Microsoft Purview DLP: delegate Copilot and Cowork policies to administrative units
summary: The briefing's policy scoping, delegation, permissions and licensing prerequisites are supported by Microsoft documentation. It correctly distinguishes the roadmap targets from Learn's rolling preview; the role-group navigation needs only an omitted page heading.

claims.claim: Purview DLP is extending administrative unit support to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention is extending Administrative Units support to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork DLP location supports administrative unit scoping.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location supports administrative units for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork.

claims.claim: Administrators assigned to units can manage scoped Copilot DLP policies without tenant-wide policy-management permissions.
claims.quote: You can scope a DLP policy for these experiences to a region or department and delegate policy management to administrators assigned to those units, without granting tenant-wide policy management permissions.

An administrative unit is a subset of the Entra directory, typically organised by business group or geography.
claims.quote: Administrative units are subsets of your Microsoft Entra ID directory ... These collections are typically created along business group lines or geopolitical areas.

claims.claim: A policy can be scoped to one or more administrative units.
claims.quote: Unrestricted administrators don't have to select administrative units as part of the policy configuration. They can keep the default of the entire directory or select one or more administrative units.

claims.claim: The policy-scoping route is Microsoft Purview portal > Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Admin units.
claims.quote: go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. ... Select the Custom template, then Custom policy, and enter a name and description. ... On the Admin units page, select the administrative units for the policy.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy-name> -PolicyRBACScopes <administrative-unit-GUIDs> to create a unit-scoped policy.
claims.quote: The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the DLP policy. ... The PolicyRBACScopes parameter specifies the administrative units to assign to the policy.

claims.claim: PolicyRBACScopes accepts administrative unit Entra object GUIDs, with multiple values separated by commas.
claims.quote: A valid value is the Microsoft Entra ObjectID (GUID value) of the administrative unit. You can specify multiple values separated by commas.

claims.claim: Restricted administrators can select only their assigned units and manage policies within that scope.
claims.quote: An administrative unit restricted administrator can select only their assigned units and manage policies within that scope.

claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can select units or retain Full directory for an organisation-wide policy.
claims.quote: An unrestricted administrator can scope policies to administrative units or keep Full directory to apply a policy across the organization.

claims.claim: The entire directory is the default policy scope for unrestricted administrators.
claims.quote: Unrestricted administrators ... can keep the default of the entire directory or select one or more administrative units.

claims.claim: After selecting units, administrators select the Copilot location and include or exclude users and groups within those units.
claims.quote: Select the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location and choose the users and groups to include or exclude within the selected administrative units.

claims.claim: Assigning administrative units to role-group members requires the Role management role.

claims.claim: The unit-assignment route is Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users > Assign admin units.
claims.quote: On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: Include the omitted page heading in controls[1].ui and its rendered table: 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users > Assign admin units'. The cited permissions page gives this heading; member selection and its Select confirmation remain procedural details rather than path labels.

claims.claim: No automation operation for assigning units to a Purview role-group member is documented.

claims.claim: Assigning administrative units to a Purview role-group member makes that administrator restricted.
claims.quote: After you assign administrative units to members of the role groups, these restricted administrators can't see and edit existing policies.

claims.claim: Entra roles override scoped Purview assignments and leave access unscoped for overlapping capabilities.
claims.quote: When both scoped Microsoft Purview role assignments and Entra roles are present, Entra roles always take precedence, and scoping applied through Administrative Units doesn't restrict the user's effective permissions for overlapping capabilities.
